newsitem.title: USA: Knoll settles suit over thyroid treatment.
newsitem.headline: Knoll settles suit over thyroid treatment.

text.p: Knoll Pharmaceutical Co said Monday it had reached an agreement in principle to settle a series of class action lawsuits involving its thyroid medication, Synthroid.

Knoll said it will contribute $98 million to a fund to cover payments to class members, legal fees and related expenses. If there are more than five million eligible claimants, Knoll said it will contribute additional payments to the settlement fund up to a maximum of $135 million.
The action stems from an $8.5 billion suit filed in April accusing Knoll and its parent, Germany's BASF AG, of suppressing a medical study to control the U.S. market for thyroid drugs.

The suit alleged that Knoll, BASF and Boots Co Plc concealed a university study concluding that Synthroid, a synthetic version of the compound levothyroxine, was no better than cheaper, generic brands.
The suit said Knoll controls 84 percent of the $600 million-a-year levothyroxine market in the U.S.
In May, shares of BASF fell more than four percent immediately after news of the lawsuit was widely distributed, and Boots shares fell 20-1/2p from a high of 740p five days earlier.
Knolls said the proposed settlment remains subject to execution of a definitive agreement and court approval.
A statement from the company Monday evening said, "The settlement in no way implies or acknowledges any wrongdoing" and added that the court had not ruled on the merits of the claims.
